where in M a later hand has added the letter r, by which θερμερῶπιν [hot-looking] is indicated, which is in many copies and which the scholiast seems to have read, who explains it by θερμήν [hot]. In Hesychius there is θεμερῶπις: ἐρασμία ἀγχόνη [modest-looking: lovely noose], which Sopingius thought should be written ἐρασμία αἰσχύνη [lovely shame], so that the gloss is taken from a verse of Aeschylus. The same Hesychius explains θέμερον [modest] by σεμνόν [revered] and θεμέρη [modest] by σεμνή [revered].
